title: Business skills: which written processes do agents follow, and who controls them?
summary: Hold: the Skill Sharing Role requirement is overstated as preventing all access, although Microsoft also documents general and direct sharing. The controls and REST operations are documented, but the page also confuses feature availability with record existence and generalizes Sales agent session guidance to all routes.

claims.claim: Business skills are natural-language instructions describing the steps, required information and business rules for a type of work.
claims.quote: Each skill describes how to complete a specific type of work—the steps involved, the information required, and the business rules that apply.

claims.claim: Business skills are stored as records in Dataverse.
claims.quote: Records of instructions, scripts, and resources that agents can discover and use to do things more accurately and efficiently.

claims.claim: Business skills are not executable code and guide agents like a written employee procedure.
claims.quote: Business skills are not executable code. They contain natural-language instructions that guide agent behavior, similar to how you might document a process for a new employee.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[0]; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off the environment Work IQ setting makes business skills unavailable in that environment.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. If you turn off this setting, these features aren't available in the environment.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants.

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Nonproduction environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft deferred the plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.claim: Manage feature settings still lists the earlier Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) setting as Off by default.
claims.quote: Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences | When On, allows reusable business context business skills to be used by your agents. | Off

claims.claim: The business skills pages name no licence specific to skills.
claims.quote: To use skills through Business Applications in Work IQ, you need access to a supported Copilot experience or connected agent.

claims.claim: Creating skills requires a Dataverse environment with Work IQ enabled.
claims.quote: A Dataverse environment with Work IQ enabled by a Power Platform administrator.

claims.claim: Creating skills requires permissions to create business skills in the environment.
claims.quote: Permissions to create or use business skills in the environment.

claims.claim: Work IQ skill use requires access to a supported Copilot experience or connected agent, and the creation page links Work IQ licensing requirements.
claims.quote: To use skills through Business Applications in Work IQ, you need access to a supported Copilot experience or connected agent.

claims.claim: Work IQ API use is paid for through usage-based Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ cost is tracked by consuming experience rather than a dedicated business applications category.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.

claims.claim: Work IQ consumption supporting a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.
claims.quote: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.claim: Direct Work IQ calls from coding agents or custom integrations appear under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.claim: The applicable Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat entitlement includes business-data grounding.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario.

claims.claim: Spending policies set consumption limits for the consuming experience.
claims.quote: Spending policies let you choose the users and services covered, set a shared monthly limit, add a per-user limit, and receive alerts as consumption approaches a threshold.

claims.claim: A request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps, so task cost varies.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.claim: A credit rate specific to following Dataverse business skills is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "business skills" "credit" "rate"; "business skills" "Copilot Credits" rate pricing audit events sharing admin. Read understand-costs, Work IQ overview/API overview and Copilot Studio billing-rate search excerpts; no Dataverse skill-specific rate found.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Two-role trap; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access through a shared security role requires both that role and Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: Users who access a skill through a Dataverse security role must have both the selected role and the Skill Sharing Role security role.

claims.claim: A user missing Skill Sharing Role never gets a skill shared with a security role.
claims.quote: Owners can provide general access to everyone in the environment, share with selected Dataverse security roles, or provide direct access to specific users or groups.
claims.fix: Replace the Two-role trap bullet with: 'Access through a Dataverse security role requires both the selected role and Skill Sharing Role; either alone is not enough for that route.' The requirement does not rule out general or direct access. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-business-skill-overview.

claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.quote: Searched: "business skills" "audit" "events". Read Work IQ overview, business skills overview/create, skill table messages and Dataverse auditing search excerpts; general logging is documented, but no named skill retrieval/following audit event was found.
